newsitem.title: USA: Lawyer for PSI says to appeal Honeywell case.
newsitem.headline: Lawyer for PSI says to appeal Honeywell case.

text.p: An attorney for PSI Repair Services Inc, of Livonia, Mich., said the company plans to appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court a court ruling involving it and Honeywell Inc.
"Unquestionably, PSI will review its options and, at this time, plans to appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court," said Rodger Young, attorney for PSI.

Minneapolis-based Honeywell Inc said Tuesday that the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit affirmed a lower court's ruling against PSI's claim that Honeywell's policy on replacement of failed circuit boards violated antitrust laws.
Honeywell will not sell component parts for its circuit boards to customers or third parties, it said.
PSI asserted the policy prevented it from competing against Honeywell in repair services, Honeywell said.

According to Honeywell, the court found that "no violation has occurred because Honeywell's policy for replacement of failed circuit boards was consistent and generally known. The court also decided that Honeywell's pricing structure and service policies were well-known and clear," the company said.

In a statement, Young said, "PSI was disappointed in the opinion ... The court ultimately hinged its decision on an issue that was not briefed by the parties -- the adherence by Honeywell to the restrictive policy."
